topics.topic: What is a Large Language Model (LLM)?
topics.definition: A Large Language Model is an AI model trained on large amounts of text to understand and generate human language.
tips: LLMs learn language patterns from training data.

topics.definition: NLP enables computers to understand, interpret and generate human language.
tips: LLMs are an important part of modern NLP.

topics.definition: Training data is the collection of text used to train an LLM.
Parameters are learned values that determine how the model makes predictions.
tips: Larger models usually have more parameters.

topics.definition: The context window is the amount of information an LLM can process at one time.
tips: Longer context windows handle larger inputs.

topics.definition: LLMs are used for chatbots, coding, summarization, translation and many other tasks.
tips: Choose prompts suited to the task.

topics.definition: LLMs can produce incorrect or incomplete answers and depend on the quality of prompts.
Use clear prompts, verify outputs and evaluate model performance regularly.
